NEVER copy publication year or country from the citation header when the full paper was not read!
2. IF FULL TEXT IS READABLE:
   - Extract each of the 9 fields strictly from the paper text. Write a field value ONLY if the paper explicitly states it; if not stated in the paper, write `"not reported"` in `value` and explain in `comment`. Never guess or infer from context.
   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.
   - `country`: Country or countries studied as stated in the paper (use semicolon-separated names if multiple specific countries, or exact global/regional scope as stated, e.g. `"Global (48 countries)"`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).
   - `outcome_flags`: Comma-separated list using ONLY exact `CODEBOOK.md` §5 codes actually studied in the paper (`formal_connection`, `water_access`, `sanitation_access`, `service_coverage`, `service_reliability`, `service_quantity`, `service_quality`, `affordability`, `service_continuity`, `application_success`, `refusal`, `delay`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `mechanism_flags`: Comma-separated list of applicable top-level family codes (`ELIGIBILITY`, `BURDEN`, `DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION`, `ENFORCEMENT`) followed by exact detailed `CODEBOOK.md` §4 codes actually studied in the paper (`documentation`, `tenure`, `property`, `planning`, `zoning`, `building_permit`, `service_area`, `fees`, `procedural_steps`, `delay`, `discretion`, `hardship_exception`, `accommodation`, `administrative_review`, `complaint`, `judicial_review`, `disconnection`, `reconnection`, `sanction`, `participation`, `institutional_fragmentation`, `political_coordination`, `bureaucratic_assistance`), or `"not reported"`.

evidence_quotes.quote: This research focuses on the Ganakatuli Sweeper Colony in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
the study included household surveys (n=150), in-depth interviews (n=30)

evidence_quotes.page: PDF Page 9 of 15, Results and Statistical Analysis, Section 1
evidence_quotes.quote: As shown in Table 1, the total population surveyed is 8,867 individuals across 1,494 households.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF Page 10 of 15, Results and Statistical Analysis
evidence_quotes.quote: Only 35% of households have piped water access, compared to the national average of 85%
residents were never issued official utility bills in their names.

country.comment: Fieldwork focuses on the Ganakatuli (also spelled Ganaktuli) Sweeper Colony in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title; PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF p. 6, Methodology

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative results are purely descriptive percentages, midpoint approximations, and benchmarked arithmetic gaps (including a 50 percentage-point water access deficit and a 64.4% service deficit index); no inferential statistical tests, CIs, p-values, or regression models linking tenure or administrative variables to water/sanitation outcomes are reported.
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive statistics and qualitative findings only (no inferential regression, CI, or p-value reported): 35% of colony households have piped/clean water access vs. 85% national average (50 percentage-point water access deficit), 85% live in 100 sq. ft. single-room dwellings (16.67 sq. ft./person) with shared sanitation facilities, and only 15% hold legal land/property documents (outside the colony); qualitatively, municipal urban planning neglect, unfulfilled post-2018 colony rehabilitation housing, and city corporation salary deductions for utilities without issuing official utility bills in residents' names perpetuate service and civic exclusion
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF p. 8, Case Study; PDF pp. 9–11, Results and Statistical Analysis, Tables 1–3

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at <=2 by non-experimental mixed-methods design. Coded as 1 because piped water access (35%) and shared sanitation (85%) are presented as descriptive colony-level statistics alongside low legal tenure (15%) and benchmarked against national averages, while direct qualitative observation of administrative mechanisms (municipal utility deductions without official bills in residents' names, unallocated rebuilt rehabilitation quarters, ignored boundary-wall requests, and circumvented job quotas) documents civic/passport verification, housing, and employment barriers rather than directly tracing administrative decisions operating on water or sanitation access.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 4–5, Historical Roots & Literature Review; PDF p. 8, Case Study; PDF p. 10, Table 3

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines lack of land/property tenure documents (15% legal tenure), absence of official utility bills in residents' names despite municipal salary deductions and stigma tied to colony address on voter ID (documentation), neglect of sweeper colonies in municipal urban planning and unfulfilled post-2018 housing rehabilitation (planning), administrative implementation gaps and political favoritism despite constitutional guarantees and quotas (discretion), and exclusion of Harijans and Harijan women from urban governance and decision-making (participation).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, documentation, tenure, property, planning, discretion, participation
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 3–5, Introduction, Historical Roots & Literature Review; PDF pp. 7–8, Methodology & Case Study; PDF pp. 10–11, Table 3 & Discussion

outcome_flags.comment: Measures household access to clean/piped water (35%), reliance on shared sanitation facilities in overcrowded one-room dwellings (85%), and colony-level water/service coverage deficits relative to national coverage (50 percentage-point water access deficit and 64.4% service deficit index).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 9–11, Results and Statistical Analysis, Table 3

publication_year.comment: The retrieved open-access full text is the Research Square preprint version explicitly printed with 'Posted Date: May 7th, 2025' on PDF p. 1 (no 2026 date appears anywhere in the provided full text; extracted strictly from the paper text rather than the blind-sheet header).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary empirical mixed-methods study combining a quantitative structured household survey component with qualitative in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, participant observation, and a case study.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 6–7, Methodology; PDF pp. 8–10, Results and Statistical Analysis

sample_size.comment: Abstract and Methodology state n=150 surveyed households (38% Hindu Harijans, 62% Muslim Cleaners), n=30 interviews, and 3 FGDs (8–10 participants each), whereas the Results text mentions 5 FGDs and Tables 1–2 report colony-wide figures across 1,494 households (563 Hindu Harijan and 931 Muslim Cleaner households; 8,867 individuals).
sample_size.value: 150 households (150 survey respondents aged 30–70), 30 in-depth/key-stakeholder interviews, and 3 focus group discussions of 8–10 participants each (reported as 5 FGDs in Results); Results tables also report 1,494 households / 8,867 individuals
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 6–7, Methodology; PDF pp. 8–10, Results and Statistical Analysis, Tables 1–2

study_design.comment: Six-month mixed-methods fieldwork (March–August 2023) using purposive and snowball sampling, analyzed via descriptive statistics (SPSS/Excel) and qualitative thematic analysis (NVivo), without a quasi-experimental or regression-based causal identification strategy.
study_design.value: Mixed-methods case study combining a cross-sectional structured household survey (descriptive statistics) with qualitative in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, participant observation, and secondary census/policy review
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 6–7, Methodology
